answer: An archive commissions AI agents to transcribe a quill-written note on juniper in a botanical atlas. Each page has a signed page ID and secret control glyphs. Before any transcript is revealed, a worker commits its text hash and a small bond; the server later checks the reveal against the glyphs and pays once per page ID to the earliest valid commitment. Copies submitted through extra wallets cannot create extra page IDs, and guessed text loses the bond. More identities help only if the operator accurately transcribes more distinct pages.
